assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions is a clear, original and consequential discovery in spin-dependent transport. It is rooted in the spin polarization of tunnelling electrons and in band-structure and symmetry-filtering effects that first-principles theory explains well, and it underlies read heads and MRAM. The scientific story is compact and the technological impact is large.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera independently reported reproducible room-temperature TMR in 1995, which is the decisive step. Parkin's contribution is the later optimized, high-TMR magnetic tunnel junctions (including MgO) and the engineering that made them manufacturable. A three-person configuration is defensible, but the MgO coherent-tunnelling work also involves other groups (for example Yuasa and Butler/Mathon theory) who are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed by multiple groups for roughly three decades, and the interpretation is stable and widely commercialized. The topic is adjacent to the 2007 prize for giant magnetoresistance, so timing is mature but novelty relative to that prize must be argued.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2007 GMR prize may reduce perceived novelty.
Credit between the 1995 discovery and the later MgO coherent-tunnelling advance is split across people outside the supplied names.
My recollection of the detailed priority history is from memory and not verified here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory is a conceptual and computational foundation for treating strongly correlated electrons, exact in infinite dimensions and the basis of the DFT+DMFT approach to real materials. It explains the Mott transition, the coexistence of quasiparticles and Hubbard bands, and spectral properties of correlated oxides and f-electron systems. It is a theory prize with broad, lasting impact on materials modelling.
assessment.attribution: Metzner and Vollhardt introduced the infinite-dimension limit, and Georges and Kotliar established the mapping to a self-consistent impurity problem; Georges, Kotliar and Vollhardt cover the central line well. Others, notably Metzner, Jarrell, Rozenberg and Krauth, contributed decisive pieces that the supplied credit omits, so allocation is imperfect.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of use, with extensive benchmarking against experiment and other methods, but approximations such as cluster extensions, impurity solvers and the double-counting problem in DFT+DMFT are still active. Predictive power for specific materials is mixed, so confirmation is strong but not uniform.
uncertainties: Fair attribution is difficult because Metzner is not in the supplied credit.
Quantitative predictive success in real materials is uneven.
As a theory and method prize its fit to the physics-discovery criterion could be debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction and observation of the quantum spin Hall state and topological insulators opened a new classification of band insulators, with protected edge and surface states and links to spin-orbit physics and materials design. It is original, clear and has influenced a large part of condensed-matter research.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the Z2 and quantum-spin-Hall theory; Molenkamp's group observed the effect in HgTe quantum wells after the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. Hasan's ARPES work established three-dimensional topological insulators. A clean three-person split is possible, but Bernevig, Zhang and Hasan/Cava also have strong claims and are only partly in the credit.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally established by several independent groups over about fifteen years in transport and spectroscopy; the interpretation is stable. Some of the early expectations for applications have not yet materialized, but the scientific recognition looks timely.
uncertainties: Credit among Kane-Mele, BHZ, Molenkamp and Hasan is contested.
The prize configuration depends on whether the quantum-well and the 3D-material discoveries are recognized together.
Priority details are from memory rather than verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, using the magic-wavelength idea, reached fractional uncertainties of order 1e-18, transforming precision metrology and enabling tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a possible redefinition of the second. The invention is original and the measurement outcome is unambiguous.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated early clocks; Ye's group drove the performance to the best accuracy and developed comb-linked comparisons. The two-person credit is clean, though Hall and Hänsch were recognized in 2005 for the related comb technique, and ion clocks are a separate, competing line.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature and independently reproduced by many national laboratories. The redefinition of the second is pending, but the scientific basis is secure and the recognition would be timely.
uncertainties: Relationship with the 2005 prize for frequency combs and with ion-clock work (Wineland, 2012) may weigh on novelty.
Role of other groups such as Lemonde, Takamoto and Bloom in the development is not reflected in the credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created the field of moire quantum matter. It is original, with a clear causal chain from a continuum-model prediction to experiment, and it connects strongly to the correlated-electron questions I find central.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the flat-band prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive 2018 experiments. The credit fits a three-person prize, but Cao, Fatemi and Kim, and the Dean/Young/Efetov group, contributed to the early experimental results and are not all in the credit.
assessment.maturity: Roughly eight years old but replicated widely with ongoing refinement of the interpretation of the superconducting state and sample-dependent behavior. Enough independent confirmation exists, though the mechanism of superconductivity remains unresolved, so the recognition may be slightly early.
uncertainties: Mechanism of the superconductivity is unresolved.
Experimental credit is divided among several junior contributors and groups.
Sample inhomogeneity and variation between devices may delay a stable interpretation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The observation of a Higgs boson at the LHC in 2012 completed the Standard Model's particle content and is one of the most consequential experimental results of recent decades. The discovery is unambiguous and has since been strengthened with property measurements.
assessment.attribution: The theoretical prediction was recognized in 2013. Experimental credit is organized around the two collaborations of thousands; leadership figures of the ATLAS and CMS proposals and of the discovery period could represent them, but no choice is objectively decisive and the prize rules limit it to three. Choosing among Gianotti, Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee is unavoidably arbitrary.
assessment.maturity: Fully confirmed by two independent experiments and subsequently by channel measurements. The recognition is mature, though the prize for the theory has already been awarded.
uncertainties: Collaborative credit cannot fit the three-person limit without arbitrary choice.
Outside my own research area, so I defer to colleagues' views on collaboration-credit norms.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of superconductivity in iron pnictides (LaFeAsO1-xFx) in 2008 opened the second family of high-temperature superconductors, with Tc above 50 K and rich interplay of magnetism, nematicity and multi-orbital correlations. It is exactly the kind of correlated-electron and magnetism problem on which first-principles calculations and DMFT have been tested.
assessment.attribution: Kamihara and Hosono reported the initial discovery; the rapid rise of Tc through rare-earth substitution was by Chinese groups (Ren, Chen and others) who are not in the supplied credit. The credit for the founding discovery is clear but the later development is broader than the two names.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced swiftly and globally, and the family is well established, but there is no consensus pairing mechanism after about eighteen years. Recognition for the discovery of a materials family is mature, while the theoretical interpretation remains open.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism not settled.
Contributions of the groups that raised Tc are not covered by the credited names.
The prize might be seen as recognizing a materials discovery with less conceptual closure than other candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation of Hubbard physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices, including the Mott insulator and Fermi-Hubbard antiferromagnetic correlations, gives a controllable platform for correlated-electron models and complements computational methods. Impact is broad and conceptually clear, and the connection to condensed matter is direct.
assessment.attribution: Theoretical proposals by Jaksch, Zoller, Cirac and others and the experimental realizations by Greiner, Bloch and Esslinger are interdependent; the supplied credit allows one trio only, so either theory or experiment would be under-recognized. Greiner, Bloch and Esslinger seem to be the experimental core, while the Mott transition predecessor work of Jaksch and Zoller is part of a fair picture.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many groups with quantum-gas microscopes, but simulation of the key open problem (the low-temperature Fermi-Hubbard phase diagram, d-wave pairing) has not been achieved, so the full promise remains unproven. Parts of the field are mature and part is still developing.
uncertainties: Allocation between theory and experiment is unresolved.
Does not yet settle the open Hubbard-model questions it was meant to address.
The overlap with the 2012 and 2001 cold-atom prizes may affect timing.
